description:
## Question

From the NIF survey and the Nx boundary, which workloads become the yardstick the kernel subset must express? How many, which categories, which existing catalog entries stay, and which candidates are ruled out (e.g. because Nx or an Erlang BIF already covers them).

comments.text:
Resolution: six target workloads, one per NIF-survey category. Each reproduces a named package's job and data shape, uses that package's pure-Elixir twin as the baseline, its NIF as the native comparison, and is measured at a small and a large size (crossover reported where cheap):
1. WebSocket masking: bandit_native vs Bandit ws_mask/2; 125 B frame / 1 MiB.
2. PCM mixing with clipping, N streams: Membrane NativeAdder vs ClipPreventingAdder; 10 ms chunk / 1 s.
3. HLL update_many over pre-hashed u64s: ex_data_sketch Rust vs Backend.Pure; 100 / 100k items.
4. Cosine top-k over f32 embeddings: vettore distances vs plain Elixir and Nx (carries the verdict's Nx row); 1k x 384 / 100k x 384.
5. Batched Levenshtein, one query vs N candidates (existing fuzzy_search): fuzler / ex_strsim vs our Elixir; 1k / 234k words.
6. Gorilla XOR-float encoding: gorilla_stream C++ vs its pure encoder; 100 / 1M points.

Order of trying (guides, does not bind; dependencies only for real technical blockers): string distance (works today) -> masking (bitwise ops, defk-w38) -> cosine top-k ([f32]) -> PCM ([i16]/[i32]; state between calls stays in Elixir for now) -> HLL (waits on opt-in wrapping arithmetic, defk-dtw.10; leading-zero count) -> Gorilla (bit reinterpretation, variable-length bit output). Choosing a workload commits to an attempt: a feature that breaks the one rule leaves it out_of_scope, but nothing that would work well is excluded up front; a workload that turns out to fit can be added any time.

Supporting examples (in the catalog, not counted toward go/no-go): rolling_stats, geo_nearest, image_blur.
Permanent exclusions: plain CRC32 (:erlang.crc32 BIF), dense linear algebra (Nx; matrix multiply defk-9p6.3 becomes the verdict's traps entry).
Expansion candidates, listed in a new verdict section "Where defk could grow", not built in this map: persistent mutable structures via kernel-owned resources; the scanning half of parsers (delimiter offsets as [i64]); CRC32C and pixel-format conversion; per-pair string distance and tiny calls if call overhead drops; n-body; replacing a wrapper by writing the library itself in defk (e.g. keccak, lz4, base58), with research deciding which libraries are small and loop-shaped enough.

title: Choose the target workload set
